h1: Lightroom alternative for Mac and Windows: develop and manage RAW photos
lead: LightKoja is a Lightroom alternative for Mac and Windows. The app manages your photos locally and develops RAW files with sliders for highlights and shadows, color grading and masks. Try LightKoja free for 3 days, then pay €19.99 a month or €79 once.
highlights: RAW from Canon, Nikon, Sony, Fuji
Local on Mac and PC, no cloud

features.title: A library for large photo collections
features.text: Sort photos into albums and folders, by date, in smart albums or stacks. Give 0 to 5 stars, flags and color labels, and search precisely, for example for “rating:>3 iso:>800”. When culling, LightKoja shows a RAW file’s embedded preview in around 0.1 seconds, and jumping to the next photo takes about 50 milliseconds (as of November 2026).

features.title: Color and color grading
features.text: You set white balance automatically, with the eyedropper or via temperature and tint; there’s also Vibrance, which protects skin tones, Saturation and an HSL color mixer with 8 color ranges. Three color grading wheels tint shadows, midtones and highlights separately. Press V to turn a photo black and white, and use the 8-channel black-and-white mix to control how bright the sky or foliage become.

features.title: Masks for sky, subject and gradients
features.text: Paint with the brush, drag linear or radial gradients, or select areas by brightness, color, sky, subject or background. You combine several selections by adding, subtracting or intersecting, and each mask has 17 sliders of its own. LightKoja detects sky and subject with classic image processing, not with AI.

features.title: Light, curves and effects
features.text: Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites and Blacks work with local tone mapping that recovers blown-out skies without gray halos. There are also tone curves for RGB and individual color channels, plus Texture, Clarity, Dehaze, Vignette and Grain.

features.title: Presets and copying settings
features.text: LightKoja comes with ready-made looks like “Golden Hour” or “Teal & Orange”, each with an amount slider from 0 to 200%. You create your own presets, and copy or sync selected settings to many photos at once. XMP presets can be opened too.

features.title: Crop, retouch, HDR, panorama
features.text: You crop freely or with fixed aspect ratios, straighten photos with Upright and retouch distracting spots by removing, healing or cloning with automatic source selection. You merge bracketed exposures into HDR images, and several shots into panoramas or HDR panoramas. For more elaborate image editing, [PhotoKoja](/software/photo-koja) is included in the same price.

features.title: Export for web, print and archive
features.text: Export as JPEG, PNG, TIFF, flat PSD, WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL or DNG, with size settings, maximum file size, output sharpening, naming templates and watermarks. You save print layouts as color-managed PDFs, and contact sheets as PDFs too.

features.title: Local, fast, non-destructive
features.text: All edits run through a 32-bit floating-point pipeline with a wide color space, and your original files are never changed. Processing happens on your Mac’s GPU: on an Apple M4 Pro, a slider change on a 24 MP RAW takes around 4 milliseconds (as of November 2026). Photos and catalog stay on your Mac or PC, without an account and without a cloud.

switching.title: Switching from Lightroom to LightKoja: how to try the alternative
paragraphs: A lot feels familiar. The library with albums, stars and flags on the left, the sliders on the right: Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites and Blacks, with Curve, Color, Color Grading and Effects below. You may already know some keyboard shortcuts too: V for black and white, \ for the before view, Y for side-by-side comparison. The interface is in English; under “Edit > Language” you can switch it to another language.

You can partly bring your edits over from Lightroom Classic. LightKoja reads and writes XMP sidecars and reads the develop settings stored in them (crs:). If you run “Save Metadata to File” in Lightroom Classic first, these XMP files sit next to your RAWs. Lightroom Classic now partly stores extensive edits in separate ACR files, so check on a few photos what comes across. Because LightKoja never changes your originals, the way back always stays open.

Good to know: measured camera color profiles aren’t included. For Sony, Nikon, Panasonic, Fujifilm and Canon CR3, colors are estimated from camera JPEGs; other RAWs use a neutral color matrix. LightKoja doesn’t come with profiles for automatic lens correction, and AI denoise is in the works. Generative fill, Super Resolution, video editing and the Map and Book modules aren’t included, and you save print layouts as PDF instead of using the macOS print dialog. LightKoja is in active development: you get updates and new features automatically and free of charge.

How to test the switch in 3 days: download the Kojalytics Launcher, install LightKoja and import a copy of a recent shoot. Check that your camera RAWs open cleanly, edit a few typical photos and export them the way you need them. If it suits you, choose between €19.99 a month for all 13 apps and a [one-time purchase for €79](/software#preise). Our [guide to canceling Adobe](/ratgeber/adobe-abo-kuendigen) covers what to watch out for when ending your Adobe subscription.

faq.q: Is LightKoja a full Lightroom alternative?
faq.a: For many photographers, yes: library, RAW development, masks, presets, HDR, panorama and export are included. Not included are measured camera color profiles, profiles for lens correction, Super Resolution and generative fill. LightKoja is in active development, and you get updates free of charge. So test LightKoja with your own photos before you decide.

faq.q: Which cameras and file formats does LightKoja support?
faq.a: LightKoja opens RAW files from Canon (CR2, CR3), Nikon (NEF), Sony (ARW), Fujifilm (RAF incl. X-Trans), Panasonic and Leica (RW2, RWL), Pentax (PEF), Olympus (ORF) and Samsung (SRW), plus DNG, JPEG, PNG, TIFF, WebP, JPEG XL and PSD. LightKoja doesn’t develop some CR3 variants, compressed ORF and SRW files, or Nikon HE NEF; in that case it shows the embedded preview, if there is one. You can export as JPEG, TIFF, PSD, AVIF, JPEG XL and DNG, among others. Whether your iPhone photos in HEIC format open is best checked in the free trial.

faq.q: Can I bring my edits over from Lightroom?
faq.a: Partly. LightKoja reads and writes XMP sidecars and reads the develop settings stored in them (crs:), and it also opens XMP presets. In the trial, check on a few typical images how accurately your settings come across. The guide [Lightroom alternatives without a subscription compared](/ratgeber/lightroom-alternative-ohne-abo) has more on switching.

faq.q: Can I get LightKoja without a subscription?
faq.a: Yes. For €79 once, you get LightKoja and the 12 other Koja apps as a one-time purchase, valid on up to 3 devices. For comparison: Lightroom costs $119.88 a year on an annual plan paid upfront. If you’d rather pay monthly, take the subscription for €19.99 a month, which you can cancel online any time with no fee: [see both options](/software#preise).

faq.q: Does LightKoja run on my Mac, and in which languages?
faq.a: LightKoja is a universal app for Macs with Apple silicon and with Intel processors. Processing happens on the GPU: on an Apple M4 Pro, exporting a 24 MP RAW at full size takes around 0.3 seconds (as of November 2026). The interface is in English and is available in 18 languages in total. LightKoja also runs on Windows; it’s not available for the iPad or the browser.

faq.q: What do I get for my money?
faq.a: Kojalytics develops, tests and signs the Koja apps and delivers them with a launcher, activation and automatic updates. You get updates and new features free of charge, plus support by email. You also get 12 more apps for the same price. Your photos and your catalog stay on your Mac or PC, and you can back up the catalog at any time.
